messages:
pagerduty: HIGH - incident triggered: autoscaler_queue_backlog (service: scale-controller) — https://pagerduty.example/INC12345
incident-bot: paging on-call in #eng-oncall due to backlog > 1000 for inference-requests queue
maya: acked — I'm on call, looking now
alex: seeing 10k queued requests, 95p latency ~8s, 5% 429s. UI: https://console.internal/queues/inference-requests
maya: checking HPA and cluster-autoscaler. `kubectl get hpa -n inference` shows desired=1/current=1 targetCPU=80%
jin: logs from scale-controller show repeated errors: `failed to provision node: quotaExceeded` and `insufficient capacity`
samir: cloud quotas were changed in the last maintenance window, could be related. Samir to infra?
samir: I'm in infra channel. quick check: node-pool autoscale policy still there, but service-account used by ca-controller lost roles after PR #582 merged
maya: that would explain no new nodes. can someone confirm exact error snippet? pasting tail of controller log: ```E0320 12:34:01 scale.go:142] scale attempt failed: rpc error: code=PermissionDenied desc="permission denied: compute.instanceGroups.resize"```
alex: :eyes: that is a permissions issue, not capacity. PagerDuty firing was correct — backlog grew because autoscaler couldn't act
maya: temporary mitigation plan: 1) manually resize nodepool to add +3 nodes, 2) apply rate limit to public API, 3) patch service account roles. I'll coordinate
jin: manual resize ok, but who has console rights? I can run gcloud if you paste the exact command
maya: running: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize redwood-infer-pool --region us-central1 --size 6` — doing it now
incident-bot: manual action recorded: `gcloud resize` executed by maya at 12:38UTC
samir: also opening a cloud support ticket for quota/roles change, tagging infra-iam
alex: applied temporary rate limit on the hosted API: `/admin/rate-limit set inference 0.6` — should drop ingress by ~40%
maya: nodepool resize returned success, nodes are provisioning. watching queue drain
jin: meanwhile, adding a temporary routing rule to send lower-priority traffic to dedicated pool: `route:set inference low-priority -> dedicated-pool`
alex: queue length dropping: 10k -> 3.2k in 4 minutes, latency 8s -> 3s, 429s down to 1.2%
maya: PagerDuty: acknowledged incident, will escalate to eng-sre if regression within 15m
pagerduty: incident acknowledged by maya (12:39UTC)
maya: brief customer impact summary for ops-team: Hosted API experienced elevated latency and increased 429 errors for ~12 minutes affecting ~7% of requests, root cause: autoscaler lacked permissions to resize nodepool after recent IAM change. Workaround: manual node resize + temporary rate limiting. Full fix requires IAM role restore and postmortem
jin: taking on-call handoff at 12:45UTC — I'll own follow-ups: restore service-account roles, add unit tests to detect role drift, and file RFC for safer permission changes
maya: handoff accepted, leaving notes in incident doc: https://incidents.internal/INC12345
incident-bot: incident transitioned to "stabilized". follow-up assignees: jin, samir, infra-iam
samir: created jira RED-789 (restore autoscaler IAM + alert on permission changes) and linked to incident
alex: CS notified, customer-facing note drafted in #customer-success, ticket CS-1122 attached
maya: thanks team — great quick work. follow-up items: patch creds, verify autoscaler metrics alerting, add runbook snippet for manual resize. :thumbsup:
jin: ack — will update when IAM fix is deployed
incident-bot: closing chat loop, moving discussion to #postmortems when postmortem doc ready
